tasks.short: Find out today's duties and rules, supervise recess, lunch and trips, and report incidents.

steps.what: Substitute teacher reads the duty rota and school rules on arrival from a paper folder
Substitute teacher supervises students at recess
Substitute teacher accompanies field trips with regular staff
Substitute teacher writes a note about incidents for the duty manager

tasks.design: The school gives substitutes a short login to the student information system ({OTHER}) with today's duties, rules and an incident form, instead of a paper folder and loose notes. Supervising recess, lunch and trips stays fully in person.
tasks.previous_blocker: Substitutes had no system access, so information came on paper and incidents on notes.
tasks.enabler_now: Pupil records systems support role-based access and incident forms.
tasks.still_hard: Supervision is presence; short-term access must be granted and removed every time.
tasks.human_edge: Keeping unfamiliar children safe and calm on the first day.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes; the substitute is informed faster.

reach.learn: Whether a short login replaces the paper folder.

evidence.claim: Records apps with role-based access hold pupil records confidentially.
Pupils' data needs data minimisation; substitutes see only what the day requires.

assumptions: Boundary: from arrival to incidents reported; incident follow-up is outside.
Input contract: duties and rules kept by the school administrator; short-term access granted by the administrator; fallback is the paper folder.
Duty manager time is outside the substitute's savings.
unknowns: Whether the school grants substitutes system access.
research_questions: Do incidents reach the regular staff sooner?

incremental.description: Substitute teacher logs in and learns the form.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Schools without substitute logins keep paper folders, and supervision itself is unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read the teacher's plan, prepare role-play cards, lead the social skills lesson, handle conflicts and leave a note.

steps.what: Substitute teacher reads the regular teacher's plan for the social skills lesson
Substitute teacher makes role-play cards and examples for the lesson

loop.input: The lesson goal (for example, saying no politely or solving a quarrel) and the pupils' age group.
loop.output: Six short role-play situations with roles and a discussion question each.
loop.check: Each situation must practise the stated goal; wording must stay within an age-appropriate word list; no names of real pupils; the substitute reads every card before printing.
loop.stop: One draft and one redraft; then the substitute uses the plan's own examples.
loop.why_not_simpler: Writing believable situations for one goal and age is creative work; a template only gives the card layout.

steps.what: Substitute teacher leads discussion and role play on communication and etiquette
Substitute teacher helps students through conflict resolution during the day
Substitute teacher leaves a handwritten note for the regular teacher

tasks.design: A bounded step drafts role-play situations for the lesson goal and age group, which the substitute reads before printing; no pupil data enters it. A short handover form in {DOCS} replaces the handwritten note; the lesson and conflict talks stay in person.
tasks.previous_blocker: Substitutes had little time to prepare examples for a class they did not know.
tasks.enabler_now: Language models draft short scenarios, and Dutch lesson editors already rewrite text at another level.
tasks.still_hard: Teaching social skills works through the relationship, which a substitute must build fast.
tasks.human_edge: Getting a strange class to talk honestly about a quarrel.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in decision rights; preparation is quicker.

reach.learn: Whether drafted role plays suit small groups.

evidence.claim: A Dutch lesson editor rewrites text at another level and pulls word lists with definitions.
AI that evaluates learning outcomes is high-risk; drafting role-play cards is not.

assumptions: Boundary: from reading the plan to the handover note; follow-up by the regular teacher is outside.
Input contract: lesson plan and goal left by the regular teacher; handover form set up by the school; fallback is the plan's own examples.
No pupil data enters the drafting step.
The lesson and conflict talks do not change.
unknowns: How often social skills lessons fall on substitute days.
research_questions: Do drafted role plays work as well as the regular teacher's own?

already_counted.description: Substitute teacher reads every drafted card before printing.

incremental.description: Substitute teacher fills in the handover form.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Plans that already include role-play material leave little to prepare.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Find out who needs help, work with pupils one to one or in small groups, pick extra exercises and note progress for the teacher.

steps.what: Substitute teacher works out from the teacher's notes who needs help with what
Substitute teacher tutors students one to one and in small groups
Substitute teacher looks for extra exercises at the right level
Substitute teacher writes progress notes for the regular teacher

tasks.design: With a short substitute login, the group plan in the student information system ({OTHER}) shows who needs help on which goal, extra exercises come from the school's levelled practice materials or the lesson editor's level rewrite, and progress goes into a handover form. The tutoring itself stays with the substitute.
tasks.previous_blocker: Substitutes worked from scraps of notes and searched for exercises themselves.
tasks.enabler_now: Pupil records systems hold group plans, and Dutch lesson editors rewrite exercises at another level.
tasks.still_hard: A substitute does not know the pupils; live suggestion tools for tutors exist in trials but need training.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing where a pupil gets stuck and explaining it another way.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in decision rights; less searching before helping.

reach.learn: Whether shared group plans help outside tutors focus.

evidence.claim: A Dutch lesson editor rewrites text at another difficulty and pulls word lists.
In a randomised trial with about 900 tutors, live AI suggestions raised topic mastery by 4 percentage points, 9 for lower-rated tutors.
AI that evaluates learning outcomes in education is high-risk from 2 December 2027.

assumptions: Boundary: from finding who needs help to progress noted; marking is outside.
Input contract: group plan kept by the regular teacher; levelled practice materials licensed by the school; short-term access granted by the administrator; fallback is the teacher's notes.
No pupil data enters outside tools.
unknowns: Whether the school grants substitutes access to group plans.
research_questions: Do substitutes reach the right pupils sooner with the group plan?

already_counted.description: Substitute teacher checks the level of picked exercises.

incremental.description: Substitute teacher handles login and access issues.
School administrator grants and removes substitute access.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Schools that give substitutes no access keep the paper route.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Find the tests and homework left by the teacher, hand them out, collect work and track who handed in, and leave it for marking.

steps.what: Substitute teacher looks for the tests and homework the teacher left
Substitute teacher distributes and explains the homework assignments
Substitute teacher collects work and ticks who handed in on a class list
Substitute teacher leaves the collected tests with a note for the teacher
Regular teacher marks the collected work

tasks.design: Homework sits in the class's electronic learning environment ({OTHER}), where the substitute sees what is due and who has handed in online. Paper tests are still handed out and collected; the hand-in list comes from the environment instead of ticking names.
tasks.previous_blocker: Assignments were in a folder and hand-in was tracked on paper.
tasks.enabler_now: Electronic learning environments hold assignments and online hand-in.
tasks.still_hard: Tests on paper stay physical; substitutes need short-term access.
tasks.human_edge: Getting a class to take a test seriously for someone they do not know.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes; less searching and ticking.

reach.learn: Whether online assignments make cover days smoother.

evidence.claim: Electronic learning environments hold assignments and online hand-in lists.
Pupils' data needs data minimisation and role-based access.

assumptions: Boundary: from finding assignments to handing work to the teacher; marking is outside.
Input contract: assignments posted by the regular teacher; short-term access granted by the administrator; fallback is the folder and class list.
Regular teacher time is outside the substitute's savings.
Handing out and explaining do not change.
research_questions: Do more pupils hand in work on cover days when it is online?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Classes that still set homework on paper keep searching and ticking.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The substitute teacher keeps supervising, teaching and helping; finding information and paperwork shrink with short-term access.
skills_to_grow: Using a school's systems quickly with limited access
role.ambitious_version: A substitute who walks into any school and is fully informed within five minutes.
